_comment: CANONICAL-WINNER ENFORCE set. A CLOSED, curated list of DISTINCT model families that must WIN over a disagreeing raw_family when the model ID itself names the family (the ID-derived family equals one of these). This covers BOTH (a) the own-family-enforce ledger (a provider mislabels a distinct model as its parent: aion/magnum as 'llama', mixtral/pixtral/voxtral as 'mistral', wizardlm/inflection as 'gpt', intellect as 'glm', qwq as 'qwen', weaver/owl as 'alpha') AND (b) the vendor/org-namespace leak (raw_family is the ID's ORG, not a family: nousresearch->hermes, allenai->olmo, liquid->lfm). In reconcileIDDriven, when the ID-driven family differs from raw_family AND the ID-driven family is in this set, the ID-driven decomposition (family+variant+version+modifier) is adopted wholesale — the raw mislabel/org is discarded. The set is closed (no per-name runtime guessing): only an ID whose own leading token resolves to one of these distinct families triggers the override. Sorted alphabetically. The ledger treats codellama as its own family. 'meta' is handled separately via family_aliases (meta->llama), not here. inkling and kling are one three-way collision of class (a): the vendored catalog ships raw_family "ling" verbatim on ALL 14 rows -- Thinking Machines' 6 Inkling rows AND the 8 klingai/kling-v* video rows -- so both were folded onto inclusionAI's unrelated Ling family. The IDs themselves are correct and always were (vercel spells its rows klingai/kling-v2.5-turbo-i2v, leading 'k' intact), so the ID-driven decomposition is authoritative and the two ledger rows split all 14 without a single exact-ID pin.
